Ultimately, in a fed-batch process lasting 2 days, the ethylene glycol titer reached 36.5 mM, equivalent to 2.3 g/L (Figure 36B). Figure 36. (A) Anaerobic formaldehyde consumption within 2 hours. (B) long-time fed-batch bioconversion of ethylene glycol production, with initial 10 mM formaldehyde and 20 mM formate. 52 Additionally, we observed that formate consumption decreased linearly at the initial stage, corresponding with a linear increase in ethylene glycol. Once formate was fully consumed, the rate of ethylene glycol production noticeably slowed. These data highlight the importance of formate as an energy source for ethylene glycol biosynthesis.
